fields.expected: I'm an undergraduate at Johns Hopkins studying Applied Mathematics & Statistics and Economics, class of 2029, and most of my work has been building products and machine-learning systems end to end. Right now I work on the machine-learning core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system at Summer Atlantic Capital / SAC Nexus, where I own the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI detection service, temporal sequence models over event streams, and a retrieval-augmented explanation layer. A lot of that work is less about model accuracy than operational usefulness, since a detector that fires constantly just creates a second problem for analysts. I also co-founded Open Health Intelligence and led the technical work on ClarityAtlas, an iOS health app built with Swift, SwiftUI, and Supabase that estimates sleep passively from phone motion and interaction signals; we shipped it into a live Hopkins pilot with 30+ users and were selected for the Pava Spark Accelerator and NSF I-Corps. Earlier, I founded SnapSort, an AI photo-sorting product I built on Flask and AWS and grew past 300 users while owning pricing, positioning, and go-to-market.
